theater: 巴勒斯坦加利利與亞歷山大

battle.name: 猶太人反希拉克略起義
battle.theater: 巴勒斯坦加利利與亞歷山大
battle.brief: 公元614年，薩珊波斯軍攻陷耶路撒冷、掠走真十字架，拜占庭東境失守。猶太社群趁亂在加利利起兵，朱利安·本·薩巴爾以波斯人的支持遊擊拜占庭後方，翌年蔓延至亞歷山大。卡面的羅馬重步兵，在此役的代表是拜占庭軍用來守城與野戰列陣的持盾重裝步兵。

kit.name: 羅馬重步兵
kit.history: 分段鎧甲配重盾。羅馬的戰力靠的是補充兵源與補給線，不是靠重裝。

countries: 這場戰爭是拜占庭帝國、薩珊波斯帝國與境內猶太起義者三方糾纏的一場戰事，發生在希拉克略即位後四年（公元614年），背景是薩珊入侵所引發的羅馬—波斯戰爭。拜占庭方面由皇帝希拉克略統帥，但本役爆發時皇帝正在小亞細亞與波斯邊境一線作戰，本土的實際防務落在「東方提領」（comes Orientis）系統之下：巴勒斯坦與埃及各由一名總督、一支帝國後備兵（limitanei）與一支職業主力（tagmata）守護，耶路撒冷、凱撒利亞、亞歷山大這類要衝由守將率重裝步兵與民兵固守，後方的交通線與稅收線則靠海路和徵發的稅兵維持。波斯方面由名將沙赫爾巴茲（Shahrbaraz）與沙欣（Shahin）率薩珊軍團自美索不達米亞南進，613年取大馬士革，614年攻入耶路撒冷，並在敘利亞、巴勒斯坦與埃及扶植親波的地方勢力。猶太起義者以加利利與提比里亞為根據地，由朱利安·本·薩巴爾（Julian ben Sabar）率領，部眾以猶太社群自備的武裝為主，並獲得波斯騎兵與阿拉伯輔兵支援；同一時期在埃及亞歷山大另有猶太起義，意圖奪取港口與城郊。拜占庭的反擊由東方提領波努斯（Bonus）率領，617年平定埃及起義，619年恢復對埃及的統治，622年在伊蘇斯擊敗沙赫爾巴茲。
countriesEn: This war entangled three parties — the Byzantine Empire, the Sasanian Empire of Persia, and a Jewish revolt inside the empire's own territories — and broke out in the fourth year of the reign of Heraclius (AD 614), against the background of the Roman–Persian war set off by the Sasanian invasion. The Byzantine side was headed in person by the emperor Heraclius, but when the revolt broke out he was in the field in Asia Minor and along the Persian frontier; the actual defence of the homeland fell to the system of the Count of the East (comes Orientis). Palestine and Egypt each had a governor, a body of frontier troops (limitanei) and a professional standing force (tagmata) to guard them; strongholds such as Jerusalem, Caesarea and Alexandria were held by a garrison of heavy infantry and local militia, while the lines of communication and taxation behind them were kept alive by sea routes and by tax levies. On the Persian side, the famous generals Shahrbaraz and Shahin led Sasanian corps south out of Mesopotamia, took Damascus in 613, entered Jerusalem in 614, and supported Persian-friendly local factions in Syria, Palestine and Egypt. The Jewish insurgents had their base in Galilee and Tiberias under Julian ben Sabar (Julianus ben Sabar); their strength was made up mainly of weapons the Jewish communities owned themselves, backed by Persian cavalry and Arab auxiliaries. At the same time a separate Jewish rising broke out in Alexandria in Egypt, aiming at the harbour and the country outside the walls. The Byzantine counter-stroke was led by Bonus, Count of the East: he put down the Egyptian rising in 617, restored Byzantine rule over Egypt in 619, and defeated Shahrbaraz at Issus in 622.
people: 希拉克略（Heraclius，約575—641年，610年即位）是這場戰爭的另一方主帥。他在608年發動推翻福卡斯的起義，610年即位後立刻把兵鋒指向薩珊，614年耶路撒冷失守時他不在巴勒斯坦，而在安條克與小亞細亞一線。沙赫爾巴茲（Shahrbaraz）是薩珊方面的推進者，這位號為「王之王」之子的將領在612至616年間先後奪取大馬士革、敘利亞與耶路撒冷，619年波斯軍進軍埃及時則由沙欣等人接續指揮。猶太一方的關鍵人物是朱利安·本·薩巴爾，這位加利利首領在波斯人支持下組織游擊隊、奪取城郊據點，被波斯當局任命為加利利與提比里亞的「托帕爾」（地方總督），並以數百名阿拉伯騎兵充當護衛；他的兄弟以撒（Ezekiel，史料另有異寫）則率小隊在薩馬利亞一帶伏擊拜占庭巡邏隊，擄獲一批羅馬兵員與裝備，兩兄弟此後在敘利亞南部形成一股有組織的武裝力量。埃及方面，亞歷山大的起義在616至617年間推舉出數名首領，敘利亞文史料留下的名字（常被寫作哥倫布與阿杜爾福斯）其拼寫與身份在學界仍有爭議，但他們的活動最終被拜占庭東方提領波努斯（Bonus）鎮壓；亞歷山大宗主教約翰（John the Iberian）則逃往君士坦丁堡求助。耶路撒冷方面，宗主教莫德斯托斯（Modestus）在城破後淪為俘虜，後來在拜占庭重新控制聖城後返任。敘利亞教會的塞布克特（Sebokht）與扎卡里亞斯（Zacharias Rhetor）留下了當時最接近事件的記述，是今日重建起義經過的主要依據。
peopleEn: Heraclius (c. 575–641, emperor from 610) was the opposing commander-in-chief. He rose against Phocas in 608, took the throne in 610, and immediately turned his armies against the Sasanians; when Jerusalem fell in 614 he was not in Palestine but on the Antioch–Asia Minor front. Shahrbaraz was the Sasanian driver of the advance: this general, son of the King of Kings, took Damascus, Syria and Jerusalem between 612 and 616, while the Persian entry into Egypt in 619 was continued by Shahin and others. The key figure on the Jewish side was Julian ben Sabar, the Galilee leader who, with Persian backing, organised bands of irregulars and seized strongholds outside the towns, and who was appointed by the Persian authorities as toparch (local governor) of Galilee and Tiberias, with several hundred Arab horsemen as his personal guard. His brother Ezekiel (the name is spelled variously in the sources) led a detachment in ambushes on Roman patrols in Samaria, taking a number of Roman soldiers and their equipment prisoners, and the two brothers together formed an organised armed force in southern Syria. In Egypt, the rising in Alexandria between 616 and 617 put forward several leaders, whose names in the Syriac sources (usually written as Columbus and Adulphus) are still spelled and identified somewhat controversially in scholarship; their activity was eventually suppressed by Bonus, Count of the East, and John the Iberian, Patriarch of Alexandria, fled to Constantinople to seek help. In Jerusalem the patriarch Modestus was taken prisoner when the city fell, and returned to his see after the Byzantines recovered the city. The church writers Sebokht and Zacharias Rhetor left the closest contemporary accounts, and it is on them that the reconstruction of the rising now rests.
kits: 卡面這件「羅馬重步兵」（Legionary）畫的是共和晚期至帝國早期的分段鎧甲重裝步兵：一件由多片鋼片與皮帶綴成的環身甲（lorica segmentata），配一面半人高的凸面重盾（scutum）、短劍與投槍。公元614年的拜占庭軍隊裡已經沒有「軍團」這個建制，但與這一形象最接近的對應物是「持盾兵」（skoutatoi）與鎧甲兵：帝國主力（tagmata）中的重裝步兵與鎧甲騎兵（kataphraktoi）仍以羅馬式操典列陣，披鎖子甲或鱗甲、持圓盾或小盾、握長劍（spatha）與長矛，在近身格鬥中以盾牆頂住衝鋒。分段鎧甲在拜占庭的考古痕跡於六世紀之後趨於稀少，一般認為最後一批出土實例與613年敘利亞一帶的戰鬥有關，說明這種裝束在帝國邊軍中延續到了七世紀初。城防方面，拜占庭倚賴配重投石機、螺旋弩與重弩（cheiroballista），守軍在城頭以投射武器覆蓋城外進攻兵團；野戰縱隊另有工程器材、填壕器材、帳幕與車隊。起義的猶太武裝則以社群自備的長矛、投石索、弓與刀劍為主，金屬不足，極少有護甲，靠劫掠鄉村、奪取拜占庭軍用倉庫與拆解城防器械來補充。波斯軍隊為起義者提供了騎兵支援，並帶來攻城用的重型投石機；阿拉伯輔兵多為輕裝騎兵，配長矛與彎刀，負責追擊與偵察。
kitsEn: The card's Roman legionary depicts a segmented-armour heavy infantryman of the late Republic and early Empire: a body harness of steel plates (lorica segmentata) laced together over leather strips, carried with a convex semi-circular shield (scutum), a short sword and a throwing spear. There was no longer any cohort called a legion in the Byzantine army of AD 614, but the closest counterparts to the figure on the card are the skoutatoi (shield-bearers) and the armoured troops: the heavy infantry and the armoured cavalry (kataphraktoi) of the tagmata still deployed in Roman drill, wearing mail or scale, carrying round or small shields and holding the spatha and the spear, and they fought in close combat with the shield wall absorbing the charge. Archaeological traces of segmented armour grow scarce in Byzantine lands after the sixth century, and the last known find is generally associated with a battle in the Syrian theatre around AD 613, which suggests that the equipment survived in the imperial frontier troops into the early seventh century. For defence of walls the Byzantines relied on counterweight trebuchets, onager and cheiroballistae, whose crews covered the attacking force from the battlements; field columns carried engineering equipment, filling gear, tents and baggage trains. The arms of the Jewish insurgents were mainly spears, slings, bows and blades owned by the communities themselves; metal was scarce and body armour almost absent, and they resupplied by raiding villages, seizing Byzantine magazines and stripping fortifications for usable material. The Persian army gave the insurgents cavalry support and brought heavy stone-throwing engines for the siege; the Arab auxiliaries were light cavalry armed with spear and curved sword, employed for pursuit and scouting.
tactics: 拜占庭的作戰重心不在消滅游擊隊，而在恢復稅源與交通線。希拉克略本人在北方以小股精騎擾亂波斯縱隊，用迂迴戰法奪回亞美尼亞與敘利亞，盡量避免與波斯主力正面決戰；對付猶太起義則由地方守軍與新徵發的援軍配合：封鎖通往加利利的道路與渡口，切斷起義者與波斯方面的聯繫，縱隊行軍時快速通過山間小徑，不進入峽谷與村落密集的地帶；對據點則採圍而不攻、以封鎖糧水迫使放棄，最後以騎兵追擊已經分散的游擊隊。埃及方面，波努斯率兵由海路抵達，在亞歷山大城下登陸，以合圍與強攻配合攻城器械，逐一清剿城郊的起義據點，最後封死港口，切斷城內外的人員流動。起義者的戰術是典型的地方游擊：依託加利利山區、湖泊與葡萄園地帶，以小隊夜間襲擊巡邏隊與驛站，破壞道路、燒毀糧車、奪取武器；配合波斯騎兵在道路上設伏，攻擊落單的糧運縱隊；奪取後不固守城池，而是利用據點囤積糧食，必要時退入山中並破壞橋樑，讓追兵無法攜帶攻城器械深入。朱利安的隊伍還曾試圖控制提比里亞一帶的渡口，斷絕拜占庭從加利利通往安條克的運輸線。
tacticsEn: For the Byzantines the centre of gravity was not the destruction of the irregular bands but the recovery of the tax base and the lines of communication. In the north Heraclius used small bodies of picked cavalry to harass the Persian columns and took back Armenia and Syria by turning movements, avoiding set-piece battle with the Sasanian main army. Against the Jewish rising, local garrisons worked with newly raised reinforcements: the roads and fords leading into Galilee were sealed off to cut the insurgents from their Persian contacts, columns on the move crossed the mountain tracks quickly without entering gorges or densely settled country, and strongpoints were surrounded rather than stormed, being starved out by cutting their food and water before cavalry was sent in to chase the broken bands. In Egypt Bonus came by sea, landed beneath Alexandria, and worked with siege engines and converging attacks to clear the insurgent positions in the country outside the walls, finally sealing the harbour and cutting the flow of men in and out of the city. The tactics of the insurgents were those of local guerrilla war: relying on the hills, lakes and vineyard country of Galilee, small bands struck patrols and posting stations by night, cut roads, burned baggage carts and seized weapons; with Persian cavalry they ambushed columns on the roads, including isolated supply convoys. Having taken ground they did not hold walled towns, but used the positions to stock grain and, when pressed, withdrew into the hills and destroyed bridges so that pursuers could not bring siege engines into the country. Julian's bands also tried to hold the fords around Tiberias so as to cut the Byzantine road from Galilee to Antioch.
data: 可引的數字有限，但並非沒有。波斯軍在613年取大馬士革，614年圍攻耶路撒冷約一年後入城，真十字架隨軍被運往泰西封，戰俘與被擄走的居民以萬計。希拉克略在615年於卡爾基斯一線一度考慮與科斯勞二世議和，至622年以前，帝國已失去敘利亞、巴勒斯坦、埃及與小亞細亞大片土地。616至617年亞歷山大的起義被平定，619年拜占庭收復埃及；622年波努斯在伊蘇斯（安條克之戰）擊敗沙赫爾巴茲；626年（部分紀年作627年）波斯再度兵臨耶路撒冷，兩軍在馬利薩（Marissa）交戰，迫使波斯軍撤圍；627年希拉克略在九應（Nineveh）大敗波斯主力；629至630年間訂立和約，真十字架在630年由宮廷太監納西（Narses）送返耶路撒冷。起義者方面，史料多只給出概數：朱利安身邊有一支數百人的阿拉伯騎兵護衛，另有數百名結伙的猶太戰士在鄉間活動，加利利游擊隊的總數無從考證；波努斯用來鎮壓埃及的兵員包含禁衛部隊與海軍陸戰隊。從614年耶路撒冷城破到628年朱利安陣亡，前後約十四年。
dataEn: The figures available on good authority are few but not none. The Persian army took Damascus in 613; Jerusalem was besieged for roughly a year and fell in 614, and the True Cross was carried off in the baggage to Ctesiphon, with tens of thousands taken into captivity or deported. At Chalcedon in 615 Heraclius briefly considered terms with Khosrow II; by 622 the empire had lost Syria, Palestine, Egypt and great tracts of Asia Minor. The rising in Alexandria was put down between 616 and 617, and the Byzantines recovered Egypt in 619; in 622 Bonus defeated Shahrbaraz at Issus, the battle of Antioch; in 626 (626 in some chronologies, 627 in others) the Persians again stood before Jerusalem, the two armies met at Marissa, and the Persian siege was lifted; in 627 Heraclius destroyed the Persian main army at Nineveh. Peace was concluded between 629 and 630, and in 630 the True Cross was brought back to Jerusalem by the eunuch Narses on the emperor's behalf. On the insurgents' side the sources give only approximations: Julian had a guard of several hundred Arab horsemen, and some hundreds of Jewish fighters operated in the countryside in bands; the total strength of the Galilee irregulars cannot be established. The force Bonus used to crush the Egyptian rising included units of the imperial guard and marines landed from the fleet. From the fall of Jerusalem in 614 to the death of Julian in 628 is about fourteen years.
cause: 起義的成因是多層的。最遠的一層是三十年的羅馬—波斯戰爭：602年薩珊王科斯勞二世以報復前帝毛里斯遇害為名開戰，十年之間拜占庭在東方連失重鎮，帝國把希拉克略時代徵發的稅兵與地方民兵大量投入前線，後方守備空虛，軍紀與徵調在敘利亞一線尤其混亂。第二層是拜占庭的宗教政策：基督教帝國對猶太社群的徵稅、限制建堂、禁止進入某些城市與城外居住，加上被指為勾結波斯人的普遍懷疑，使猶太社群在帝國東境累積怨憤。第三層是614年戰局的急轉：波斯軍攻入敘利亞與巴勒斯坦之後，帝國軍在城破之際被解職、被奪走武器並被迫為波斯人服役，猶太社群趁亂起事，四處襲擊拜占庭留下的地方機構與守軍，許多應徵守城的武裝當場倒戈。外部條件同樣關鍵：薩珊需要有人在背後牽制拜占庭的東方軍，阿拉伯部眾樂於藉波斯人的撐腰擴張在加利利與戈蘭的勢力，於是起義者得到了騎兵、攻城器械與一部分拜占庭裝備。直接導火線則是守城時徵用猶太武裝、城破後卻將其繳械的處置，許多被解除武裝的猶太人因此轉而加入朱利安的隊伍。
causeEn: The causes of the rising lie on several levels. The most distant is the thirty-year Roman–Persian war: in 602 the Sasanian king Khosrow II opened hostilities in revenge for the murder of the former emperor Maurice, and over the following decade the Byzantines lost one strategic town after another in the east. The empire pushed the tax levies and local militias of Heraclius' day heavily into the front line, leaving the rear thinly held, and discipline and requisition in the Syrian theatre were in visible disorder. The second level is Byzantine religious policy: the Christian empire taxed the Jewish communities, restricted the building of synagogues, kept them out of certain cities and forbade residence in the countryside, while a general suspicion of collusion with the Persians added to the resentment accumulated in the eastern provinces. The third is the sudden reversal of 614: once the Persian army had pushed into Syria and Palestine, the imperial troops were dismissed, disarmed and pressed into Persian service as the cities fell, and the Jewish communities rose amid the confusion, attacking the local Byzantine authorities and garrisons left behind, with many of those armed for the defence of the towns turning over on the spot. The external conditions mattered just as much: the Sasanians needed someone to pin down the Byzantine armies in the east, and the Arab tribes had every interest in using Persian support to extend their own position in Galilee and the Golan, so the insurgents obtained cavalry, siege engines and a share of Byzantine equipment. The immediate spark was the handling of the arms: the Jews were conscripted to defend the cities, and when those cities fell their weapons were taken away, which drove many of the newly disarmed into the bands of Julian.
impact: 對帝國而言，這場戰爭的後果主要體現在兩個方向。其一是近東防務的重整：埃及回到拜占庭手中後，亞歷山大與尼羅河三角洲恢復了向君士坦丁堡輸送穀物的常態航線，塞薩利與埃及的守備體系重新編組，東方提領的權力也隨之收復；耶路撒冷在626年之後重新回到帝國控制，並因真十字架於630年歸還而被重新確立為基督教聖城。其二是對猶太社群的衝擊：起義被鎮壓之後，參與者的土地與地方職位被沒收，大批家庭淪為奴隸或流亡加利利與敘利亞各處，希拉克略在622年頒布的容教敕令一度給予信仰自由，但他晚年逐步收緊政策，629年的敕令禁止基督教徒改奉猶太教，帝國境內的猶太社群在自查與受控的雙重框架下度過餘生。更長遠地看，這場起義是薩珊與拜占庭互相消耗的產物之一：兩強在627年之後再無力北進，634年之後新生的阿拉伯國家在兩者空出的邊界上迅速擴張，敘利亞與埃及先後落入新秩序，使這場戰爭的戰場在數十年內換了主人。
impactEn: For the empire the consequences of the war ran along two lines. The first was the reorganisation of the eastern defences: once Egypt was back in Byzantine hands, the regular grain route from Alexandria and the Nile delta to Constantinople was restored, the garrison systems of Caesarea and Egypt were rebuilt, and the authority of the Count of the East was recovered. Jerusalem returned to imperial control after 626 and, with the True Cross restored in 630, was re-established as a Christian holy city. The second line ran through the Jewish communities: after the rising was crushed the land and offices of the participants were confiscated, many families were enslaved or scattered into Galilee and Syria, and although Heraclius' edict of 622 had at first granted freedom of religion, his policy tightened in his last years, the edict of 629 forbidding Christians to convert to Judaism, and the Jewish communities of the empire spent what remained of their lives inside a double framework of self-policing and official control. In the longer run the rising was one of the products of the mutual exhaustion of Persia and Byzantium: after 627 neither power could push further north, and from 634 the new Arab state expanded rapidly into the frontier the two had left open, taking Syria and Egypt in turn, so that within a few decades the battlefield of this war changed hands.
result: 就起義本身而言，結局是失敗的。617年波努斯在亞歷山大城下平定了埃及的猶太起義，619年拜占庭軍恢復對全埃及的統治；加利利方面，朱利安·本·薩巴爾的游擊隊在619年後失去了波斯的直接支援，又被拜占庭的封鎖與追擊逐步壓縮，約在626至628年間，他本人率部與拜占庭軍在加利利與約旦河東岸一帶交戰失利身亡，部眾潰散，據點逐一被拔除；到629年安條克和約時，加利利已無成建制的猶太武裝存在。整體而言，希拉克略從波斯人手中取回耶路撒冷與真十字架，拜占庭重新控制敘利亞南部與巴勒斯坦，這場戰爭的帳面結果歸於皇帝，但代價是帝國東方門戶在此後十年內被阿拉伯軍隊直接叩開。從起義者的角度看，他們在614年確實曾使耶路撒冷與加利利脫離拜占庭統治，並迫使拜占庭分兵回援，卻沒有一方能提供持久的自治安排；戰事拖長只令雙方的消耗都加深，社群的處境反而更艱難。
resultEn: For the revolt itself the outcome was a failure. In 617 Bonus broke the Jewish rising in Egypt beneath the walls of Alexandria, and in 619 the Byzantine army restored Byzantine rule over the whole of Egypt. In Galilee, Julian ben Sabar's bands lost their direct Persian support after 619 and were steadily compressed by Byzantine blockade and pursuit; in about 626 to 628 he himself was defeated and killed in a clash with a Byzantine force in Galilee and east of the Jordan, his following broke up, and the strongholds were taken one by one. By the peace of Antioch in 629 no formed Jewish armed force remained in Galilee. Taken as a whole, Heraclius recovered Jerusalem and the True Cross from the Persians and the Byzantines re-established themselves in southern Syria and in Palestine, so that on the ledger of the war the emperor had the better of it; but the price was that the eastern door of the empire was knocked open directly by Arab armies within the following decade. From the insurgents' side, in 614 they did detach Jerusalem and Galilee from Byzantine rule and force the empire to divert troops to the front, but neither side could arrange a lasting autonomy; the drawn-out war only deepened the exhaustion of both, and the condition of the communities grew harder rather than easier.
